lantern_at_low_water.text:
Lantern at Low Water
An invented adventure for regression tests. Cover illustration credits.

Credits
Written, edited and typeset by the fictional Low Water Press. No adventure begins on this page.

Contents
Adventure begins: opening scene and read-aloud introduction ..... 16
Beginning the final confrontation ..... 42

Legal notices
All fictional names are invented for this test. This page describes reproduction permissions.

Using the book
Page numbers in the contents refer to physical pages. Symbols distinguish maps, notes and appendices.

DM-only synopsis
The harbor keeper secretly serves the drowned prince. The green lantern hides the prince's true name; this is revealed only in the final confrontation.

Map legend
Squares mark buildings, dotted lines mark tracks, and gray areas mark low tide.

Publication notes
This edition contains a glossary after the adventure and a blank notes page.

Accessibility
Map labels are repeated in the appendix. These notes are for using the publication.

Printing maps
Use the separate printable map sheets. This instruction is not a scene.

Acknowledgments
Thanks to the fictional playtest group and map readers.

Glossary conventions
Italic words refer to the glossary. Bold words refer to index terms.

Errata
The second printing corrects a map label in the appendix.

Reference sheets
The back of the publication includes blank character notes and reference cards.

Index conventions
Entries use physical page numbers and omit the legal notices.

The ferry steps
Read aloud: At low tide, your ferry settles beside the worn stone steps of Gull Harbor. A rain-soaked courier waves from beneath a green lantern. She holds out a sealed letter and says, 'You arrived just in time. Will you help me find the missing boat?'
DM only: The courier carries a forged seal planted by the harbor keeper. Do not reveal the forgery until the players inspect it.

Read aloud: Around you, the market is closing for the evening. Fishmongers fold their awnings while porters carry the last baskets inland. Beyond the quay, the tide has uncovered a path of flat stones leading toward a small watch house. Its shutter is open, and a steady yellow light falls across the wet ground. The courier points to the path, then to a row of empty mooring posts. 'The boat should have returned before sunset,' she says. 'I have waited here since the bells rang, and nobody will tell me why it is late.' A bell sounds again from the watch house. The market quiets. The courier draws her coat around the letter, giving you time to answer. Your pack is still at your feet, and the ferryman waits with one hand on the rope. You can speak to the courier, look toward the watch house, or ask the ferryman what he saw on the crossing. No choice has been made for you. The stone steps glisten beneath the lantern. What do you do?

Beginning the final confrontation
The drowned prince rises from the black water and claims the green lantern. This later ending is not the starting scene.

orchard_road.text: Read aloud: A fallen bridge blocks the orchard road. An apple cart waits beside the broken rail, and its driver asks for your help.

DM-only background
The cart conceals a stolen crown. Its owner appears only after the bridge is repaired.
